newsitem.title: UK: AMERICAS CUP RETURNS TO BRITAIN -- FOR REPAIRS.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAS CUP RETURNS TO BRITAIN -- FOR REPAIRS.

text.p: Yaching's most prestigious trophy, the Americas Cup, returned to Britain on Monday -- to be repaired by the Crown jewellers.

The world's oldest sporting trophy, which was created in Britain in 1851 but has spent most of the past century in the United States, was partially destroyed by a protester in March while it was on display in New Zealand.

"The top third of the cup is very badly damaged. It's been beaten around quite severely with a sledgehammer and so there is quite of lot of restoration work to be done on that part of it," said John Heise, the commodore of the Royal New Zealand Yacht Squadron who accompanied the cup.
It was transported in a specially made Louis Vuitton case, on a first class flight from Auckland.
Jewellers Garrards estimate it will take up to eight weeks to repair the silver cup.
Militant New Zealand Maori Benjamin Peri Nathan, 27, was charged with wilfully destroying the cup on March 14.
He allegedly walked into the New Zealand clubhouse and smashed the glass showcase and trophy in an attack that caused outrage in international yachting circles.
Team New Zealand leader Sir Peter Blake, who was knighted for his efforts in securing the cup for New Zealand in 1995, said he was shocked by what happened.
"I'm saddened that someone would want to do this," he said after the attack. Heise said he expects the cup to be returned to New Zealand "as good as new."
